_comment: Seed corpus: original recipes authored for FridgeLuck suite C (own words, own structured steps; no third-party expression). Every quantity is either an author-specified gram amount (kind=weighed), a household measure with a conversion from conversions.json, or an explicit unknown (e.g. salt to taste). Animal-flesh and egg recipes carry USDA FSIS thermometer doneness checks. Claims are machine-verified by the linter's allergen scan.

steps.text: Toast the bread and keep it warm.
Melt the butter in a nonstick pan over medium-low heat.

Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt, pour into the pan, and stir slowly, scraping the base, until soft curds form. If checking with a thermometer, the eggs are done at 160°F (71°C); the yolk and white should be firm.
Spoon the eggs onto the toast and finish with black pepper.
Dice the apple (no need to peel).
Layer yogurt, apple and almonds in two glasses; drizzle with honey just before serving.
Finely dice the onion and tomato; slice the green onions.
Beat the eggs with the vegetables, turmeric and salt.

Heat the oil in a small nonstick pan over medium heat. Pour in half the egg mixture and cook flat until the top is just barely wet, about 3 minutes; if using a thermometer the center should reach 160°F (71°C).
Fold, slide onto a plate, and repeat with the remaining mixture.
Bring the stock to a bare simmer with the peas and cook 3 minutes.
Take the pot off the heat and whisk in the miso until dissolved (boiling the miso dulls it).
Divide the rice into bowls, ladle the miso broth over, and top with green onions.
Blitz the oats to a coarse flour in a blender, then mix with the flour, baking powder, sugar and a pinch of salt.
Whisk in the milk and eggs; rest the batter 5 minutes while the pan heats.
Cook quarter-cup rounds over medium heat; flip when the edges set. Egg dishes are done at 160 F on a thermometer.
Serve stacked with the maple syrup.
Blend the tomatoes with the smoked paprika and salt, then simmer in the oil in a skillet until slightly thickened, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the chips until coated; crack the eggs on top, cover, and cook until the whites are set. If checking with a thermometer, the eggs are done at 160°F (71°C).
Top with feta and cilantro and serve straight from the skillet.
Rinse the poha in a strainer until just wet; set aside to swell.
Sauté the diced potato and onion in the oil until the potato is tender, 8-10 minutes.
Add the turmeric and salt, fold in the poha gently, and cook 2 minutes more.
Finish off the heat with lime juice and peanuts.
Soften the sliced pepper and onion in the oil in a wide skillet, about 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, then the tomatoes and salt; simmer until thickened, about 10 minutes.
Make four wells and crack in the eggs. Cover and cook until the whites are set and the yolks still skim. If checking with a thermometer, the eggs are done at 160°F (71°C).
Scatter over the feta and parsley and serve from the pan.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Cook the diced potato and onion in an oven-safe skillet in the oil until tender, about 10 minutes; wilt in the spinach.
Beat the eggs with the parmesan and salt, pour over the vegetables, and cook on the hob 2 minutes to set the base.
Bake until the center reaches 160°F (71°C) on a thermometer, 12-14 minutes.
Rest 5 minutes, then cut into wedges.
Rinse and drain the chickpeas; dice the tomato and cucumber.
Toss everything with the chaat masala, lime juice, salt and cilantro; rest 5 minutes before eating.
Drain the chickpeas and crush them coarsely with a fork with the tahini, lemon juice, oil and salt.
Dice the cucumber and fold through with the parsley.
Warm the pitas, split, and stuff with the chickpea mash.
Tear the bread and toast it dry in a hot pan until edges pick up colour, 4-5 minutes.
Cut the tomatoes and cucumber chunky; slice the onion paper-thin.
Toss bread and vegetables with the oil, vinegar and salt; let stand 10 minutes so the bread drinks the dressing, then fold in the basil.
Rinse and drain the beans; toss with the cumin and a little salt and mash lightly.
Spread over two tortillas, top with the cheddar, and close with the remaining tortillas.
Cook in the oil over medium heat until the tortillas are crisp and the cheese melts, about 3 minutes per side.
Cut into wedges and serve with the cabbage dressed in lime juice.
Boil the noodles per the packet and add the edamame for the last minute; drain and rinse cool.
Whisk the tahini, soy sauce, vinegar, sesame oil and grated ginger into a dressing.
Toss noodles and edamame with the dressing; top with green onions.
Sweat the diced onion in the olive oil, add the tomatoes and stock, and simmer 12 minutes; blend smooth and season.
Butter the bread outsides, build the sandwiches with the cheddar, and cook over medium heat until crisp outside and melted inside, about 3 minutes per side.
Cut on the diagonal and serve with the soup.
Soften the diced onion and carrot in the oil, 6-8 minutes.
Add the cumin, tomatoes, lentils and stock; simmer until the lentils slump, 30-35 minutes.
Season, brighten with lemon juice, and eat thick from deep bowls.
Slice the steak thin against the grain; toss with half the soy sauce and the cornstarch.
Blanch the broccoli in boiling water 2 minutes and drain.
Stir-fry the steak in the oil in a screaming-hot wok until browned on the outside; move to a plate. To check doneness with a thermometer, medium-rare beef reads 145°F (63°C) after rest.
Add the garlic and ginger, then the broccoli and remaining soy with the sugar; return the steak and toss to gloss.
Serve over the rice.
Whisk the soy sauce, maple syrup, vinegar and ginger.
Sear the salmon skin-side down in the oil over medium-high heat 4 minutes; flip, add the sauce, and spoon it over until sticky and the thickest part reads 145°F (63°C) on a thermometer.
Serve on rice with the pan sauce and green onions.
Toss the shrimp with the cumin, half the lime juice and salt.
Sear in the oil over high heat about 2 minutes per side; a thermometer should read 145°F (63°C) at the thickest part.
Dress the shredded cabbage with the rest of the lime and salt.
Build bowls: rice, slaw, shrimp, avocado.
Press the tofu 10 minutes under a weight, cut in cubes.
Fry the tofu in the oil over high heat until crisp on two sides, about 6 minutes; remove.
Stir-fry the broccoli with the ginger 3 minutes.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, vinegar and maple with a splash of water; add to the pan with the tofu and toss until glossy.
Serve over the rice noodles.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the potato chunks in half the oil and roast 30 minutes.
Rub the chops with the oregano, garlic, lemon zest and salt.
Sear in the remaining oil 4 minutes per side, then rest. A thermometer in the thickest part should read 145°F (63°C) with a 3-minute rest.
Squeeze over the lemon and serve with the potatoes.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Toss the florets with the harissa and oil; roast until deeply caramelised at the tips, 25-30 minutes.
Pour the boiling stock over the couscous, cover, and stand 10 minutes; fork through with lemon juice.
Toast the almonds dry in a pan 3 minutes.
Pile the couscous high, top with the cauliflower, almonds and cilantro.

recipes.title: Black bean and sweet potato tacos

steps.text: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the diced sweet potato with the oil, cumin, smoked paprika and salt; roast 25 minutes.
Warm the beans with a splash of water and mash lightly.
Char the tortillas briefly in a dry pan.
Fill with beans, sweet potato, a squeeze of lime and the feta.
Brown the mushrooms in the oil in a wide pan without crowding, 6-8 minutes; add the garlic and thyme.
Stir in the orzo and stock; simmer, stirring now and then, until the orzo is tender and saucy, 12-14 minutes.
Off the heat, beat in the parmesan and season.
Boil the halved potatoes in salted water until a knife slides in, about 18 minutes.
Sizzle the garlic in the oil, add the tomatoes and salt, and simmer 8 minutes.
Lay in the cod, cover, and poach gently until it flakes and a thermometer reads 145°F (63°C), 8-10 minutes.
Tear in the basil; serve with the potatoes.
Brown the finely diced onion in the oil, 8-10 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger, garam masala and turmeric; fry 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and chickpeas with half a cup of water; simmer until thick, 20-25 minutes.
Season and serve over the brown rice.
Simmer the lentils with the turmeric and 3 cups of water until collapsing, 25-30 minutes.
Melt the butter, fry the cumin and garlic until sizzling, and pour over the dal with the garam masala and salt.
Serve over the rice, topped with green onions.
Sauté each vegetable separately with a little sesame oil and salt, keeping them in separate piles (carrots 3 min, zucchini 3 min, mushrooms 5 min, spinach wilted 1 min).
Fry the eggs until the whites are set; a thermometer reads 160°F (71°C).
Fry the rice in the hot pan until it crackles, 5 minutes.
Build the bowls: rice, vegetables in wedges, egg, a spoon of gochujang thinned with soy.
Roast the cubed eggplant with half the oil at 425°F (220°C) until soft, 25 minutes.
Fry the garlic, ginger and curry powder in the rest of the oil for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and coconut milk; simmer 8 minutes, then fold in the eggplant and warm through.
Finish with lime and salt; serve over the brown rice.
Brown the beef hard in a heavy pot, breaking it up, about 8 minutes.
Add the diced onion and garlic; cook 5 minutes.
Add the spices, tomatoes and beans; simmer covered low and slow, 25 minutes, until the ground beef reaches 160 F on a thermometer.
Stir in the corn, season, and serve topped with the cheddar.
Sweat the onion and garlic in the oil with the rosemary, 8 minutes.
Add the beans and stock; simmer gently until creamy and thick, 45 minutes.
Wilt in the kale, season, and eat over the toasted bread.
Bring the stock, rice and sliced ginger to a simmer; cook low, stirring now and then, until the rice breaks down, about 70 minutes.
Add the whole chicken breast at the 45-minute mark and poach it in the congee; lift it out, shred, and check the center with a thermometer: 165°F (74°C) for poultry.
Return the shredded chicken, season, and serve with green onions and sesame oil.
Sear the whole tenderloin in the oil in a heavy pot on all sides, about 6 minutes total.
Add the onion, garlic, cumin, tomatoes and chipotle; braise covered at a bare simmer until a thermometer in the pork reads 145°F (63°C) with a 3-minute rest, about 60 minutes.
Rest the pork, then shred and return it to the sauce.
Serve over the brown rice with lime.
